items.title: UK Court of Appeal rejects India's challenge to arbitration over Andhra Pradesh bauxite project
items.summary: The Court of Appeal of England and Wales has ruled against India in a dispute over whether a UAE investment authority can pursue arbitration over a failed bauxite mining project in Andhra Pradesh. The Court upheld an earlier ruling allowing Ras Al Khaimah Investment Authority (RAKIA) to proceed with its claims against India under the India-UAE Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT). A Bench of Lord Justices Males, Phillips and Miles dismissed India's appeal against a June 2025 judgment of the English High Court, which had overturned an arbitral tribunal's finding that it lacked jurisdiction to hear the dispute. The Court held that the government action directed at a company could qualify as action directly affecting a foreign investor's investment, even when the investment was held through a minority shareholding.
